title: Linking through unique student identifier
description: The student id submitted with the assignment is a unique identifier that can be used to link the submission data to a specific student across the system.
assumptions: Student id is globally unique within the educational system

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of student id, course, and submission timestamp creates a quasi-identifier set that could potentially link data to an individual student through analysis.
assumptions: Course and timestamp combination may not be unique across all students

title: Processing of identified information via student identifier
description: The data flow contains student id which is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, enabling direct identification.
assumptions: Student id is stored and processed by the Grades Portal Web App

title: Quasi-identifier in submission data
description: The combination of course and submission timestamp may serve as quasi-identifiers that could identify the student when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Course enrollment and submission patterns may be unique enough to identify individuals

title: Attributable submission data
description: The submission timestamp and student id can be used to attribute the assignment submission to a specific student, preventing denial of the action.
assumptions: Timestamp and student id are recorded and stored

title: Potentially sensitive work file data
description: The work file submitted may contain sensitive personal or academic information that exceeds what is functionally required for grade calculation.
assumptions: Work files may contain personal notes, drafts, or other sensitive content

title: Excessive data volume in submission
description: The full work file may be processed beyond what is needed for grade calculation, potentially including unnecessary content.
assumptions: System may store entire file rather than just metadata or grades

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their submission data (work file, metadata) is collected, stored, and potentially used beyond grade calculation.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Lack of student control over data preferences
description: Students may not have control over how their submission data is processed, stored, or shared with other parties.
assumptions: No granular consent or preference settings for data handling

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing the entire work file may violate data minimization if only metadata or grades are functionally required for the system's purpose.
assumptions: Full file storage may exceed functional requirements

title: Linking through student ID
description: Student ID is transmitted as part of the data flow, enabling linking of data to specific individuals across the system.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier within the educational system.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of student ID, course, and file reference can serve as quasi-identifiers that may link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes is unique or near-unique to individual students.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The data flow processes identified information including student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role.
assumptions: Student ID directly identifies the data subject.

title: Processing of identifier
description: Student ID is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject being transmitted through the flow.
assumptions: Student ID is a globally or locally unique identifier within the system.

title: Processing of quasi-identifier
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference constitutes quasi-identifiers that can identify the data subject.
assumptions: These attributes together are unique enough to identify individuals.

title: Data propagation to grading service
description: Personal data is propagated from the Grades Portal to the Assignment & Grading Service where it may not be strictly needed.
assumptions: The grading service may have access to more data than functionally required for its role.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to the Assignment & Grading Service, a predetermined set of parties.
assumptions: The grading service is a known, static recipient of the data.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submission data is being transmitted to and processed by the Assignment & Grading Service.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate this data flow.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the privacy policy and user interface design.

title: Lack of control over data sharing preferences
description: Students may lack control to set preferences about how their submission data is shared with the grading service.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanism exists for this data flow.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the consent and preference management system.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The data flow may process more personal data than functionally needed for the submission and grading process.
assumptions: Some of the transmitted data (e.g., file reference, requesting role) may be excessive.
uncertainty_note: Requires assessment of functional requirements to determine if all data is necessary.

title: Teacher identity linked through unique login identifier
description: Teacher logs in using a unique identifier (username, email, or institutional ID) that links their identity to the submission queue they access, enabling correlation of their actions with their personal identity.
assumptions: Teacher authentication uses a unique identifier that persists across sessions

title: Quasi-identifiers in submission queue data
description: The submission queue may contain combinations of attributes (course name, submission time, assignment type) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific students or teachers.
assumptions: Submission metadata includes multiple attributes that could be combined for identification

title: Processing of identified teacher and student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified information including teacher identity and student submission data, which are directly linked to identifiable individuals.
assumptions: System stores and processes data that can be directly attributed to specific individuals

title: Unique identifiers in submission records
description: Submission records contain unique references to student identity (student ID, username) that allow direct identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Student submissions are tagged with unique identifiers

title: Potentially sensitive data types collected
description: The system may collect data types beyond what is functionally required for grade review, such as detailed submission timestamps, device information, or metadata that could be perceived as sensitive.
assumptions: System collects metadata alongside submission data

title: Unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: Submission data may be analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is needed for the core functionality of reviewing and grading submissions (e.g., pattern analysis, automated scoring).
assumptions: System performs additional processing on submission data beyond basic retrieval

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Submission data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., administrators, other teachers, support staff) in a predetermined set.
assumptions: Data is shared with multiple internal roles beyond the requesting teacher

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data is being collected, processed, and stored by the Grades Portal Web App, particularly regarding metadata and system-side processing.
assumptions: Students are not informed about all data processing activities

title: Limited data subject control over preferences
description: Students may lack control over how their submission data is processed, stored, or shared, with limited ability to set preferences or opt-out of certain processing activities.
assumptions: System does not provide granular consent or preference controls for data subjects

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than is actually needed for the functional goal of reviewing and grading submissions, including excessive metadata or retention.
assumptions: Data collection and processing exceeds functional requirements

title: Potential invalid consent for data processing
description: Student data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent, particularly if consent is bundled, pre-checked, or not clearly communicated.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not meet regulatory standards for validity

title: Linking through student name identifier
description: Student names in the submission data serve as unique identifiers that can link the work content and submission times to specific students within the school context.
assumptions: Student names are unique within the school system and can be used to identify individual students.

title: Quasi-identifier combination linking
description: The combination of student name, work content, and submission times creates a quasi-identifier set that can uniquely identify students and potentially link their academic performance data.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes is sufficiently unique to identify individual students.

title: Profiling through work content analysis
description: Work content can be analyzed to profile student performance, learning patterns, or behavioral characteristics, potentially linking data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Teachers or systems may analyze work content for patterns or insights about students.

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The portal explicitly processes and displays identified student information including names, work content, and submission times.
assumptions: Student names are personally identifiable information that is being processed.

title: Student name as identifier
description: Student names serve as unique references to the identity of the data subject (students) in the submitted work data.
assumptions: Student names are unique identifiers within the school context.

title: Revealing attributes in submission data
description: Work content and submission times reveal attributes about students that support identification and provide insights into their academic activities.
assumptions: Work content and timing patterns can reveal information about student behavior and performance.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Student names and work content are sensitive personal data that may be more sensitive than strictly required for basic grade portal functionality.
assumptions: Some educational contexts may not require full student names or detailed work content to be displayed.

title: Fine-grained data disclosure
description: The data disclosed includes granular information (specific work content, exact submission times) that may be more detailed than necessary for teacher review.
assumptions: Teachers may not need to see exact submission times or full work content for all purposes.

title: Predetermined party access
description: Student data is made accessible to teachers (a predetermined set of parties), which is functionally necessary but should be scoped appropriately.
assumptions: Teachers are the intended recipients of this data for grading purposes.

title: Student unawareness of data sharing
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data (names, work content, times) is being displayed to teachers through the portal.
assumptions: Students may not have explicit notice about how their data is shared in the portal.

title: Lack of student control over data processing
description: Students may lack control over preferences regarding how their submission data is processed, displayed, or shared with teachers.
assumptions: Students typically cannot customize how their academic data is handled in the portal.

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: Processing of student names, work content, and submission times may exceed what is strictly necessary for the functional goal of displaying grades to teachers.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle may require limiting data to what is strictly necessary.

title: Linking through parent-child account identifiers
description: Parent account is linked to child account, enabling linking of parent's access patterns to child's educational data through unique identifier relationships.
assumptions: Parent-child account linkage is maintained in the system

title: Quasi-identifier combining parent and child data
description: Combination of parent account attributes and child grade data can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data across different contexts.
assumptions: Multiple attributes are collected that can be combined for identification

title: Processing of identified parent and child data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified information including parent account credentials and child's grade records.
assumptions: System stores and processes personally identifiable information

title: Unique identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account contains unique references to the parent's identity that can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: Account system uses unique identifiers for authentication

title: Quasi-identifier through parent-child relationship
description: The parent-child relationship combined with grade data can uniquely identify specific individuals within the system.
assumptions: Small class sizes or limited parent pool makes quasi-identifiers effective

title: Sensitive grade data collection
description: Grades are sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for the login and grade viewing functionality.
assumptions: Grade data is more sensitive than basic account information

title: Potential unnecessary data analysis
description: The system may analyze or enrich grade data beyond what is needed for the parent to view their child's grades.
assumptions: System may perform analytics or data enrichment not required for core functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on system architecture and data processing pipeline

title: Predetermined party access to grade data
description: Grade data is made accessible to the parent (predetermined party) but may be shared with other parties beyond what is functionally necessary.
assumptions: System may share data with third parties or internal services

title: Child unawareness of data access
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their grades are being accessed by the parent through this data flow.
assumptions: Child does not have visibility into parent's account access

title: Limited parent control over data processing
description: Parent may have limited control over how their child's grade data is processed, stored, or shared beyond viewing.
assumptions: System may process data for purposes beyond parent's explicit consent

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (grades, parent-child relationship) may be processed than is actually needed for the core functionality of viewing grades.
assumptions: System collects and stores more data than minimally required

title: Parent consent validity for child data access
description: Parent's consent for accessing child's grade data may not be valid under GDPR if child is considered a separate data subject with independent rights.
assumptions: Child may have independent data subject rights separate from parent
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and age of child

title: Linking through unique student identifiers
description: Grade records in the database contain unique student identifiers that can be used to link data across different views and systems.
assumptions: Grade records contain student IDs or other unique identifiers

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of attributes in grade records (student ID, course, grade, date) can serve as quasi-identifiers that enable re-identification.
assumptions: Grade records contain multiple attributes that can be combined

title: Profiling an individual through grade data
description: Grade records can be analyzed to create performance profiles of individual students, revealing patterns and trends.
assumptions: Grade data can be analyzed for patterns

title: Processing of identified data
description: The grading service processes grade records that contain identified information about students.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifiable student information

title: Processing of identifier data
description: Grade records contain unique references to student identity that are processed by the grading service.
assumptions: Grade records contain student identifiers

title: Revealing attributes in grade data
description: Grade records reveal academic performance attributes that can support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Grade data reveals personal academic information

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Grade data is considered sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required.
assumptions: Grade data is sensitive personal information

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: Building multiple views (student, parent, teacher) may involve unnecessary processing and enrichment of grade data.
assumptions: Multiple views require different data treatments

title: Excessive party exposure
description: Grade data is made accessible to multiple parties (students, parents, teachers) which may exceed functional necessity.
assumptions: Multiple parties have access to grade records

title: Unawareness of processing as data subject
description: Students and parents may not be fully aware of how their grade data is collected, processed, and shared across different views.
assumptions: Data subjects may not have clear visibility into processing activities

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control over preferences for how their grade data is processed and shared with different parties.
assumptions: Limited consent mechanisms for grade data processing

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing grade data for multiple views may exceed what is actually needed for the functional goals of the system.
assumptions: Multiple views may require more data than necessary

title: Lawfulness problems not related to consent
description: Processing of grade data may have lawfulness issues not related to consent, such as incorrect lawful ground for processing.
assumptions: Legal basis for processing may be unclear or insufficient
